Every year, the complexity of running a manufacturing company in India increases. Manufacturing businesses in India are becoming more complex every year.

Even a small error can cause bigger problems when these processes are managed by spreadsheets, disconnected programs, or manually recorded records. Delays in purchasing materials may affect production. Incorrect inventory can lead to shortages or overstocking. Managers may not be able to see where they are losing money and time due to a lack of visibility.

This is where ERP for manufacturing in India can make a significant difference.

Manufacturing ERPs bring together important business processes on one platform. They allow companies to manage their production, inventory, procurement, warehouses, financial operations, quality, and more from a central system.

For Indian manufacturers looking for a scalable and connected solution, Cloud Vellko ERP provides a manufacturing-focused ERP platform designed to bring these operations together and provide better visibility across the business.

What Is ERP for Manufacturing in India?

ERP is an acronym for Enterprise Resource Planning. An ERP system in manufacturing is designed to link the various activities that are involved in creating and delivering products. 

A typical manufacturing ERP can help businesses manage:

  • Production planning
  • Production scheduling
  • Bill of Materials (BOM)
  • Work orders
  • Inventory
  • Procurement
  • Warehouse operations
  • Quality control
  • Supply chain management
  • Finance and accounting
  • Manufacturing reports and analytics

An ERP allows you to connect all your records so that they are connected.

When a production order, for example, is created, it can be linked to the materials required, inventory availability, and procurement requirements, as well as the production progress and costs.

It gives managers a better view of the entire manufacturing operation.

Why Do Indian Manufacturers Need ERP Software?

Manufacturing businesses often start out with simple tools, such as Excel spreadsheets or accounting software. They may also use manual registers or separate applications.

When the business is small, these tools might work. Managing everything manually becomes more difficult as the number of employees, products and suppliers, locations, and production increases.

Some common challenges include:

1. Poor Production Visibility

Managers might not be able to get real-time updates on what's being produced and what has already been completed.

An ERP system centralizes production information, allowing for better visibility of work orders, schedules, and production activities.

2. Inventory Problems

Inventory can be a problem for production if it is too low or too high.

Manufacturing ERPs help businesses to track their raw materials, work-in-progress, and finished products. They also keep track of stock movement, warehouse information, and work-in-progress.

3. Procurement Delays

The availability of materials is critical to production.

By connecting procurement and production workflows, manufacturers can better understand and coordinate their purchasing activities.

4. Manual Data Entry

Employees may need to enter the exact same information several times if departments use separate spreadsheets.

It increases the risk of error and wastes time.

ERP software reduces dependency on multiple platforms by connecting business processes.

5. Limited Business Insights

To make informed decisions on production, inventory, buying, costs, and operational performance, manufacturing managers require accurate information.

Dashboards and reports in real-time can make it easier to understand and access this information.

What Should You Look for in ERP for Manufacturing India?

Not all ERP systems are designed for manufacturing.

It is crucial to determine if the ERP platform you choose can support your production workflow before selecting it for your manufacturing company.

Consider these important capabilities.

Production Planning and Scheduling

Bill of Materials Management

A bill of materials (BOM) is a list of materials and components needed to make a particular product.

Maintaining accurate BOM information for manufacturers who produce multiple products or products with various components is essential.

With central BOM management, the production team can know what materials they need before production starts.

Inventory Management

Inventory is one of the biggest areas of concern for manufacturing companies.

A manufacturing ERP should provide visibility into:

  • Raw materials
  • Work-in-progress
  • Finished goods
  • Stock movements
  • Warehouse inventory
  • Material requirements

Vellko ERP helps manufacturers better understand their production and inventory requirements by connecting manufacturing, warehouse and inventory operations. 

Procurement Management

Production cannot continue smoothly when required materials are unavailable.

An integrated ERP connects procurement with production and inventory so purchasing teams can better understand what materials are required.

This can help reduce unnecessary purchasing while making it easier to respond to production requirements.

Quality Control

When quality problems are discovered only after the products have been sold, they can be costly.

Software for manufacturing ERP can be used to integrate quality control into operational processes.

Vellko Manufacturing's ERP software includes quality management features for inspections, quality controls, defect tracking, and compliance monitoring.

Warehouse Management

Many manufacturers have multiple types of stock in different locations.

ERP systems can connect warehouse operations with procurement, production, and inventory.

It is easier to see where the materials are located and how they move through an organization.

Finance and Manufacturing

Manufacturing decisions are closely connected to financial performance.

Production costs, purchasing costs, inventory values, and operational expenses all affect profitability.

By connecting manufacturing and financial operations, businesses can get a more complete view of their costs and performance. Financial performance is closely related to manufacturing decisions.

Profitability is affected by production costs, purchasing costs, and inventory values.

Businesses can gain a better understanding of their performance and costs by connecting financial and manufacturing operations.

Who Can Benefit from Manufacturing ERP in India?

ERP software is useful to manufacturers in all industries, but particularly those that have complex operations, such as production, inventory management, procurement, or multiple locations.

Examples include:

  • Automotive component manufacturers
  • Engineering companies
  • Electronics manufacturers
  • Machinery manufacturers

  • Consumer product manufacturers
  • Industrial equipment manufacturers
  • Packaging companies
  • Furniture manufacturers
  • Electrical equipment manufacturers
  • Small and medium manufacturing units

The exact ERP requirements will depend on the manufacturing model, number of products, production complexity, number of locations, and existing business processes.

How to Implement Manufacturing ERP Successfully

The first step is to choose the right ERP. Implementation is also important.

Vellko’s manufacturing ERP approach includes understanding manufacturing processes and workflows, configuring workflows. Importing business data. Setting up BOMs. and inventory. training employees. and providing technical support.

This is 

Step 1: Understand Your Existing Processes

Identify the current management of your company's production, inventory, warehouses, and quality.

Step 2: Identify the Main Problems

Find out where you are losing money, time, or visibility.

Step 3: Configure the ERP

Create modules and workflows based on your manufacturing processes.

Step 4: Migrate Important Data

Enter all relevant information about the business, products, suppliers, BOM and inventory into the ERP.

Step 5: Train Your Team

The software must be understood by employees, not just in terms of how it works but also the connections between departments. 

Step 6: Monitor and Improve

Review reports and workflows after implementation and improve them as your business grows.
